chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and I saw Abul Hasan Musa, who was then three years old, with him was a ewe from the Meek breed, and he was holding its bridle, and he was saying to it: 'Prostrate to Allah, Who created you.' So it did that three times. A young boy said to him: 'O my master, tell it to die!' He (Musa) said to him: 'Woe to you! Do I give life and cause death? Allah gives life and causes death.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى: Title for Imam Musa al-Kadim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمَكِّيَّةُ: A specific breed of sheep known for its characteristics
key_terms.عَنَاقٌ: A young female sheep or ewe

ai.seo_question: What miracle did the young Imam Musa al-Kadhim perform with a sheep to demonstrate his status?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the early manifestation of *ismah* (infallibility) and *karamat* (miracles) in Imam Musa al-Kadhim, illustrating the Shia theological distinction between divine power and prophetic authority. By correcting the child’s assumption that he controls life and death, the Imam clarifies that while he possesses the ability to command creation through Allah’s permission, the ultimate sovereignty (*Tawhid*) remains exclusively with God. This incident serves as a foundational proof for the Imam’s unique spiritual status and his role as the perfect vicegerent who mirrors divine attributes without sharing in their essence.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (6) Abu Sulayman Ahmad bin Hawtha narrated from Ibraheem bin Iss’haq an-Nahawandi from Abdullah bin Hammad al-Ansari that Mo’awiya bin Wahab had said:

“Once I went to Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) and I saw his son Abul Hasan Musa, who was then three years old. There was a lamb with him. He said to the lamb: “Prostrate yourself before Allah, Who has created you.” He repeated that three times. A little boy said to him: “O my master, ask it to die!” Musa (as) said: “Woe unto you! Do I give life (to creatures) and make them die? It is Allah, Who gives life (to His creatures) and makes (them) die.”
